blocks.directed: Now this doesn’t mean the earlier disciplines were pointless.

blocks.text: The yogi becomes established in the conscious source itself.

blocks.text: And immersion is no longer an externally imposed operation.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja describes it as the supreme ocean of immortality, the source of the continuous flow of universal manifestation.

blocks.directed: And now, in 3.16, the yogi actually plunges into that lake through establishment in the power of Śakti.

blocks.directed: That conviction is submerged in the recognition of consciousness.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja cites the Netratantra, under the title Mṛtyujit, to describe a supreme state in which the practitioner no longer requires a fixed direction for meditation.

blocks.directed: And there is the extraordinary point.
